summary: Ban Bu is a Bangkok Noi artisan neighbourhood known for khan long hin: hammered copper-and-tin bowls polished with stone to a silver-like shine. A fifth-generation workshop has welcomed weekday visitors to observe the process. Treat this as a small, active worksite visit rather than a formal museum or pottery class.
whyGo: See a rare, labour-intensive metalworking tradition in its neighbourhood setting.
Meet artisans and understand the many stages behind the finished bowls.
bestFor: Visitors already exploring Bangkok Noi, Wat Suwannaram or Wang Lang
skipIf: You need guaranteed daily opening, a scheduled demonstration or a hands-on workshop.
You are expecting pottery; Ban Bu is known for hammered bronzeware.
duration: Allow about 45–90 minutes as a planning estimate, plus travel; the workshop does not publish a standard visit duration.
cost: No admission fee was confirmed. A May 2025 report listed finished bowls at 1,200–8,000 baht depending on size and detail; treat this as a product-price reference, not an entrance charge or guaranteed December 2026 price.
hours: A May 2025 report says the fifth-generation workshop welcomes visitors Monday–Friday. Exact hours and December 2026 holiday closures are unconfirmed. A separate local listing gives Monday–Saturday, 08:30–16:30 for the workshop, but this is not an official source; verify before travelling.
bestTime: Try a weekday morning when artisans are more likely to be working. This is practical guidance, not a confirmed daily demonstration schedule.
gettingThere: Navigate to Ban Bu / Soi Charan Sanit Wong 32, Siri Rat, Bangkok Noi. A taxi or ride-hail to the workshop is the simplest door-to-door option; the neighbourhood is near Wat Suwannaram and the Royal Barges Museum. No reliable activity-specific public-transport directions were confirmed, so check the route on the day and expect a walk through local lanes.
booking: No public booking channel or required fee was found. Because this is an operating family workshop with informal visitor arrangements, contact the workshop or a local guide ahead and confirm the date, hours and whether a demonstration is possible. Do not assume walk-in access.
accessibility: Accessibility details are unpublished. Expect a neighbourhood workshop rather than a visitor centre; narrow lanes, workshop thresholds, heat, noise and active tools may make access difficult. Ask about step-free entry and safe viewing space before setting out.
practicalTips: Ask permission before photographing people or close-up work, and keep clear of hot metal and tools.
Bring cash if you hope to buy a bowl; prices vary by size and intricacy.
Pair the visit with nearby Wat Suwannaram or Wang Lang, but confirm each venue’s separate hours.
decemberNotes: For December 2026, treat the reported weekday welcome as a lead, not a guarantee: confirm directly shortly before visiting, especially around public holidays and year-end. No special December event or seasonal schedule was verified. Bangkok is generally hot; carry water and plan for outdoor walking between stops.
uncertainties: The latest detailed visitor report located was published in May 2025; current December 2026 workshop operation and visitor access are not independently confirmed.
Exact opening hours, contact details, booking process, admission cost, demonstrations and accessibility remain unverified.
